deep.reconstruction:
The page has drawings only. It sits inside Grothendieck's 1983-84 work on 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', which are arrangements of pseudolines in the real projective plane. The paper is continuous computer-printout paper; the next page carries IBM JCL printed upside down.

Most plausible reading in modern terms:
(1) Left disc. This is the standard disc model of RP^2 (antipodal boundary points identified), or an affine chart with a line at infinity. The two green marked boundary points represent one point P, either on the line at infinity or an antipodal pair. The thin pencil curves joining them form a pencil, i.e. a sweeping family of pseudolines through P that foliates the complement of P. The red roughly vertical curves are the pseudolines of the system. They appear to be drawn so that each meets every curve of the pencil exactly once: they are 'monotone' or graph-like relative to the pencil, as in a wiring diagram.
(2) Right disc. The same configuration, but the red and brown curves wind and cross the pencil curves several times. This illustrates a system in general isotopic position that is not yet adapted to the pencil. The implicit problem is to isotope the system, or to choose the pencil, so that every pseudoline becomes transverse to the pencil with a single intersection. That is exactly the content of the 'every pseudoline arrangement is isomorphic to a wiring diagram / admits a topological sweep' statement.
(3) Centre top half-disc. The green base line has marked endpoints. The red arcs run from the base back to the base and cross pairwise once each. The dark segment on the base marks an interval of the line where several arcs land. This is the half of the picture on one side of a distinguished pseudoline, i.e. the arrangement as seen in a half-plane.
(4) Top left and bottom X. These are local pictures of a pseudoline crossing a distinguished green line transversally, and of two pseudolines crossing just above that line. They are the elementary local moves: a crossing passing through the line, as in a triangle flip or mutation, and the swaps in an allowable sequence.
(5) The next page's labels 1..5 with arrows and '1=5' fit this reading. They look like permutation and wiring sequences recording the order of the pseudolines along the pencil curves.

The purpose is to analyse pseudoline systems via sweeping pencils and the resulting sequences of permutations.
errors: No text to check; the drawings are heuristic. In the right disc it is not clear from the drawing that the tangled curves still meet pairwise exactly once (some apparent multiple crossings may just be overdrawing), so it may depict a non-generic or non-pseudoline curve family deliberately.

ideas.what: Representing a pseudoline system in the disc model of RP^2 together with a pencil (sweeping family) of curves through a marked point, with the system's pseudolines transverse to the pencil
ideas.modern_name: Wiring diagram / topological sweep of a pseudoline arrangement; spreads of pseudolines
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman (1980, wiring diagrams); Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, 1980s); Edelsbrunner–Guibas (topological sweep, 1986); Goodman–Pollack–Wenger–Zamfirescu (spreads, 1994); Levi (enlargement lemma, 1926)

ideas.what: Local pictures of crossings passing through a distinguished line (elementary moves)
ideas.modern_name: Triangle flips / mutations; swaps in allowable sequences

ideas.what: Half-plane picture: pseudoline arcs relative to a distinguished pseudoline, pairwise crossing once
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of an arrangement to one side of a line (affine/half-plane chart)

deep.surprise_reason: Exploratory drawings of standard notions (pencils/sweeps, wiring-diagram position, local crossing moves) that were all established in the pseudoline literature by the 1980s; nothing evidently new on this page.
transcription_corrections: Note that the sheet is tractor-feed computer printout paper.
The left disc's red curves are drawn as near-vertical pseudolines transverse to the pencil fan, the dark interior lines are pencil, and the marked points are greenish-olive dots.
The right disc has a few red curves overdrawn in dark brown (double tracing), not separate curves necessarily.
